For the State : Mr. V.S. Sahay, A.P.P.
 .................
14/Dated: 11/08/2023
Heard Ms. Manjulika Horo, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. V.S. Sahay, learned counsel
for the State.
2.

This petition has been filed for quashing the entire criminal proceeding including the F.I.R. in connection with Ramgarh P.S. Case No. 335 of 2016, corresponding to G.R. No. 1134 of 2016 dated 04.10.2016 registered under sections 409, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120(B) and 406 of I.P.C. and under section 11 and 13(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act, pending in the Court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ramgarh.

3. The F.I.R. has been lodged alleging therein that while preparing Award No. 02 in respect of acquisition of lands measuring an area of 1.92 acres appertaining to plot no. 2677 under khata no.
126 for the purpose of widening of NH-33 and in relation to payment thereof
, irregularities had been committed.

In course of enquiry it was revealed that the petitioner, working on the post of Assistant Praveen Kumar Sinha on the post of Head Assistant, Sanjeev Kumar Sinha as Kanoongo working in the office of the District Land Acquisition Officer, Ramgarh Anchal and others of the Land Acquisition Officer committed illegalities in the matter of payment of awarded money in respect of the aforesaid award.

4. Ms. Manjulika Horo, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that an ex-parte report dated 26.09.2016 was placed by the informant in the capacity of District Land Acquisition Officer,

1 Ramgarh to the Deputy Commissioner, Ramgarh alleging that an ward No. 02 was prepared in respect of 19 awardees whose lands were acquired for the purpose of widening of NH-33.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She further submits that it was pointed out that family/dependency certificate was not executed in the office of the Anchal Adhikari but the Anchal Office, Mandu issued a family certificate in the name of Raju Hembram.

She submits that the petitioner submitted representation before the Deputy Commissioner, Ramgarh explaining the situation with particulars of the payment in respect of the awardees justifying that he is not responsible for such alleged irregularities and illegalities in the matter of payment of compensation to the awardees.

She submits that the petitioner was unnecessarily made an accused in the F.I.R.
5.

On the other hand, Mr. V.S. Sahay, learned counsel for the State submits that the case was transferred to the Anti Corruption Bureau in view of observation made by the High Court in A.B.A.
No. 1028 of 2017 and pursuant to that present case has been registered.
6.
It appears that there are allegations of payment to wrong persons who are not entitled for the same.
Only F.I.R. is under challenge in this petition.
There are parameters of quashing the F.I.R.
No case of quashing the F.I.R. is made out.
Accordingly, this petition is dismissed.

Pending I.A, if any,
stands disposed of.
7. It is open to the petitioner to take all the grounds at the appropriate stage.

(Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi, J.) Satyarthi/
